key_insight: InstructSAM turns instruction-driven multi-instance segmentation into a set-structured query prediction task, using a learnable bank of instance queries to explicitly connect a vision-language model (VLM) to SAM3 so any natural instruction yields precise instance masks.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between high-level multimodal instructions and per-instance segmentation, enabling robust multi-instance mask prediction from arbitrary text or multimodal prompts without ad-hoc post-processing.
method: Formulate instruction-driven instance segmentation as set-structured query prediction where each query corresponds to one instance.
Inject a learnable bank of instance queries into the VLM and contextualize them with instruction and visual features (reasoning-to-instance query interface).
Pass contextualized instance queries to SAM3 to produce per-instance masks and associated outputs in a unified pipeline.
impact: Provides a scalable, modular way to combine multimodal reasoning and high-quality segmentation, simplifying building of interactive vision systems (e.g., visual assistants, image editing, robotics) that follow arbitrary instructions.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: VLM + learnable instance query bank → reasoning-to-instance interface → SAM3 → per-instance masks
Before/after example: image with natural-language instruction and resulting multiple colored instance masks
Query visualization: bank of queries being contextualized by instruction and image features (attention map style)
Performance/ablation chart: effect of query bank size and interface design on mask quality and instruction-following accuracy
paper_title: InstructSAM: Segment Any Instance with Any Instructions
paper_authors: Yuqian Yuan, Wentong Li, Zhaocheng Li, Yutong Lin, Juncheng Li
